walkthroughs.body_html:
Coordinate Systems & Time — a core area of A-Level Astronomy.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Coordinate Systems & Time brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Coordinate Systems & Time.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the full MK class of the Sun?
options: G0V
G2V
K5III
M0V

mcqs.q: Class V denotes which type of star?
options: Supergiant
Giant
Main sequence
White dwarf

mcqs.q: Why don't we have a solar eclipse every new moon?
options: The origin of black holes.
Because clouds block them.
Eclipses happen randomly.
The Moon's orbit is tilted, so it usually passes above or below the Sun's apparent position.
The observed acceleration of the universe's expansion.
The origin of black holes.
It moves backwards.
Why some galaxies are darker than others.

mcqs.q: Why was Pluto reclassified as a dwarf planet in 2006?
options: It does not clear its orbital neighbourhood of similar-sized bodies.
It moves backwards.
The origin of black holes.
It is too small to be a planet.
